column1: # Package manifest, shared by bootstrap.ps1 (scoop) and bootstrap.sh (brew/distro).
#   name     logical name, used in messages only
#   scoop    scoop identifier (bucket/package), or - if unavailable on Windows
#   brew     homebrew formula, or - if unavailable / not appropriate via brew
#   linux    distro package name (pacman/apt), or - if not applicable
# Homebrew on Linux does NOT ship GUI/WM/font packages, so anything that talks
# to the display server (i3, fonts, terminal) has to come from the distro.
# That is why brew and linux are separate columns rather than one "unix" column.
# --- language servers / debug adapters used by .config/nvim ------------------
# netcoredbg is referenced by nvim/lua/dap_config.lua (C# debugging)
# These exist to stop scoop prompting mid-install for shared dependencies.
# psmux is the Windows tmux; it reads the same tmux.conf (different plugin tail).
# stow deploys the packages on Linux; Windows uses bootstrap.ps1 junctions.
# Windows: scoop nerd-fonts bucket, per-user install, no admin.
# Linux:   brew/distro do not ship Nerd Fonts; bootstrap.sh uses getnf instead.
# Pick the -NF-Mono variant, not plain -NF or -NF-Propo: it forces single-width
# glyphs, which is what tmux/nvim column alignment depends on.
# KNOWN WART on domain-joined machines: the nerd-fonts manifest's install script
# calls Set-Acl on %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts, which fails with
# "The trust relationship between this workstation and the primary domain
# failed" when domain SIDs cannot be resolved. The failure happens AFTER the
# fonts are copied and registered, so the font works regardless - only scoop's
# bookkeeping is left saying "Install failed". `scoop uninstall` then
